test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 05 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What happens when an unbalanced force acts on an object?

options.text: The object moves without any acceleration
The object remains at rest permanently
The object always moves in a circular path
There is a change in the object’s speed or direction of motion

solution:
The correct answer is __**There is a change in the object’s speed or direction of motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an **unbalanced force** acts on an object, it causes a change in the object's motion. This change can be in the form of **speed, direction, or both**.
 
• According to **Newton’s Second Law of Motion**, the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration (F = ma). Hence, an unbalanced force leads to **acceleration** or a change in velocity.
 
• If forces acting on an object are not equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, they do not cancel each other out, resulting in a **net force** that moves the object.
 
• The nature of the movement (linear, circular, or irregular) depends on the **direction and magnitude** of the applied force.
 
• The correct statement aligns with the principle of dynamics, which states that **unbalanced forces are responsible for changing the state of motion or rest** of an object. This is a key concept in classical mechanics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Balanced vs. Unbalanced Forces:**

 
 
• Balanced forces do not cause a change in motion. For example, an object at rest remains at rest, or an object in motion continues moving at the same velocity.
 
• Unbalanced forces, on the other hand, result in a change in the object’s velocity, causing it to accelerate.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Unbalanced Forces:**
 
 
• Unbalanced forces are responsible for phenomena like starting a car, kicking a ball, or the motion of a pendulum.
 
• In space exploration, the thrust generated by a rocket engine is an example of an unbalanced force propelling the rocket forward.
 
 
 
• **Newton’s Laws of Motion:**
 
 
• Newton’s **First Law** (Law of Inertia): An object remains at rest or moves in a straight line with uniform speed unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.
 
• Newton’s **Second Law**: The acceleration of an object depends on the net force acting upon it and its mass (F = ma).
 
• Newton’s **Third Law**: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Unbalanced Forces in Daily Life:**
 
 
• A **pushing force** applied to a stationary car causes it to move.
 
• The **gravitational pull** on a falling object overcomes air resistance, accelerating the object downward.
 
• A soccer ball changes its trajectory when kicked, showing the impact of an unbalanced force.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Statement Analysis:**

 
 
• “The object moves without any acceleration” – Incorrect. Without acceleration, the object cannot change its state of motion.
 
• “The object remains at rest permanently” – Incorrect. An unbalanced force cannot maintain an object in a state of rest; it will cause motion.
 
• “The object always moves in a circular path” – Incorrect. The motion depends on the direction and magnitude of the force, not necessarily circular.
 
• “There is a change in the object’s speed or direction of motion” – Correct. Unbalanced forces cause acceleration, leading to changes in speed or direction.
 
 
 
• **Real-Life Examples:**
 
 
• In a tug of war, if one team exerts a greater force, the rope moves in the direction of the unbalanced force.
 
• A parachute slows down a skydiver because of the unbalanced upward force of air resistance.
 
• When a car accelerates, the unbalanced force from the engine overcomes the resistance forces like friction.
